title: CLI-first SDK quicksmith field notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact field notebook for a CLI-first quickstart we call "Quicksmith" — a tiny, repeatable onramp for engineers to get the Redwood SDK wired into a real app in under 10 minutes.

Audience:
- New engineers (first 10 minutes)
- Integrators doing quick POC demos
- Solutions engineers who want a deterministic set of steps to reproduce demos

TL;DR (3-minute path):
1) install: curl -sSfL https://get.redwood.ai/quicksmith | bash
2) init: redwood quicksmith init --name=my-demo --model=redwood-small
3) run local sandbox: redwood quicksmith start --hermetic
4) smoke: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"summarize: hello"}'
5) push minimal sample to cloud: redwood quicksmith deploy --preview

Why CLI-first?
- Fast feedback loop: shell + editor is the lowest-friction environment for most engineers.
- Scriptability: scripts, CI, and demo automation all rely on a stable CLI surface.
- Hermetic local sandboxing reduces support churn in early adoption.

Core objectives for this notebook:
- Provide a deterministic 10-minute path that ends with a networked request against either a local sandbox or hosted preview.
- Capture failure modes and troubleshooting heuristics so SEs can triage in <15m.
- Surface minimal telemetry to measure adoption and sticking points.
- Offer explicit fallbacks (e.g., use hosted API key) when the sandbox fails.

Quicksmith checklist (short):
- [ ] Binary installed and in PATH
- [ ] redwood quicksmith init completed without errors
- [ ] Sandbox process running on default port
- [ ] Example request returns 200 and a coherent response
- [ ] Project scaffold committed (optional)

Detailed flow and notes (notes-to-self tone):
- Init creates: quicksmith.yaml (model, seed prompt set, telemetry opt-in), a tiny express server wrapper, and a sample README with 3 requests. Keep quicksmith.yaml human-editable.
- Default mode should favor local run in a hermetic container (firejail / isolated network) so users aren’t blocked by corporate egress. 
- Provide a "light" hosted fallback: if local sandbox fails, show an unobtrusive prompt to use a temporary hosted preview token (15m lifetime).

Sample quicksmith.yaml (printed by init):
model: redwood-small-2024-quant
seed_prompts:
  - whoami: "Say your name and what you can do in two lines."
server:
  port: 8080
  route: /generate
telemetry: opt_in_prompt

Smoke test commands (for support):
- ps aux | grep quicksmith
- tcpdump -n -i lo port 8080 (if response not reaching client)
- REDWOOD_LOG=debug redwood quicksmith start --hermetic (re-run with debug logs)

Failure modes & triage heuristics:
1) Binary install fails (permission / PATH): suggest curl | sudo or manual unzip; check shell RC.
2) Sandbox exits immediately: inspect quicksmith.log; typical cause: missing container runtime or GPU driver mismatch in private deploy setups. Suggest start --no-gpu.
3) Requests hang: confirm route + port; curl -v to see connect vs read timeout. If connect OK but read stalls, check model warmup step in logs (KV cache priming).
4) Low-quality responses: ensure seed_prompts present; fallback option is to switch model to a larger variant via quicksmith switch-model command.

Telemetry plan (minimal):
Event names (short strings):
- sdk.quicksmith.installed
- sdk.quicksmith.init.completed
- sdk.quicksmith.start.local
- sdk.quicksmith.start.fallback_hosted
- sdk.quicksmith.example_request.success
- sdk.quicksmith.example_request.failure
Properties to capture (only on opt-in):
- model (string), mode (hermetic|hosted), duration_ms (int), error_code (string if failure), platform (mac|linux|win), cohort (canary|general)
Privacy notes: telemetry must be opt-in during init (explicit prompt) and defaults to off in private/on-prem installations.

Metrics to track (product):
- time_to_first_success_request (median in seconds)
- percent_of_inits_completing_local_sandbox
- percent_using_hosted_fallback
- repeat_run_rate within 7 days (indicates adoption)
- top-3 failure reasons (from error_code)

Rollout and gating idea:
- Ship CLI alpha to internal beta: 2 SEs + 4 FAEs for 2 weeks. Collect time_to_success and friction notes.
- Canary: 5% new signups offered Quicksmith in-dashboard prompt. If success metrics are within thresholds, expand.

Support runbook (for SEs):
1) Ask for quicksmith.yaml and quicksmith.log
2) If logs missing, ask to re-run start with REDWOOD_LOG=debug and send tar of logs
3) If sandbox fails due to container runtime, ask to run start --no-container and provide OS + kernel info
4) If they accept hosted fallback, create a temporary preview token and confirm example request success then open issue for local failure triage

Developer ergonomics heuristics (opinionated):
- Keep defaults minimal and optimistic: no telemetry, CPU-friendly models, small docker images.
- Provide a single "one-liner" install but ensure it drops a human-readable onboarding doc in ~/quicksmith/README.md.
- Make commands idempotent and safe to re-run (init should detect and offer to keep existing files).

Sample common commands (reference):
- Install: curl -sSf https://get.redwood.ai/quicksmith | bash
- Init: redwood quicksmith init --name=my-demo
- Start hermetic: redwood quicksmith start --hermetic
- Debug logs: REDWOOD_LOG=debug redwood quicksmith start --hermetic > qs-debug.log 2>&1
- Use hosted fallback: redwood quicksmith start --use-hosted --preview-token=<token>

Open questions (brainstorm fragments):
- Should the CLI attempt to auto-detect GPU drivers and offer a guided mitigation, or is that too invasive?
- How aggressive should the one-liner be about touching ~/.bashrc? Prefer echoing an instruction rather than auto-editing.
- Do we allow an opt-out "no-telemetry-ever" flag for enterprise installs, or rely on install-time policy?

Next steps (short roadmap):
- (2 days) Prototype: basic init + hermetic start with a tiny express wrapper + example request. Owner: Marcus.
- (1 week) Add hosted preview fallback flow and temp token generator. Owner: Emily.
- (2 weeks) Add telemetry opt-in prompt, instrument events, and wire to internal analytics. Owner: Hiro.
- (3 weeks) Internal beta with 6 SEs/FAEs, collect metrics and run 10 adoption interviews.

Notes to self: keep this notebook narrow and friction-free. Resist adding too many flags on day-1. Goal: hit a predictable 10-minute success loop that can be shown to a PM or demoed in a sales call.

References and links: see linked_artifacts for Linear and PRs. Also refer to "hermetic sandbox pattern" doc in confluence (devexp/hermetic-sandbox-pattern).

Change log: v0.1 draft — initial notebook and checklist (2025-01-14). v0.2 — added telemetry plan and rollout sketch (2025-02-27).
summary: Field notebook for a CLI-first Quicksmith quickstart: aims, 10-minute path, checklist, troubleshooting heuristics, telemetry plan, rollout steps, and next actions.
